summary: American conservative activist Phyllis Schlafly, a secret John Birch Society member, helped push the Republican Party rightward from the 1950s, led the campaign that defeated the Equal Rights Amendment and built anti-feminist, anti-gay culture-war politics.

evidence.note: Birth in St. Louis and family background; covered span starts at her birth
Runs Claude Bakewell's 1946 congressional campaign, her first political job
Own congressional run and upset primary win; treated as start of her consequential career
Partnership with Admiral Ward, books urging nuclear superiority and first-strike capability
Long segment on the John Birch Society, its founder and its conspiracy worldview
Letters show her John Birch Society membership from 1959, later kept secret
Extended background on Barry Goldwater and his anti-integration politics
John Birch Society bulk-bought her 1964 book to distribute as propaganda
Founds STOP ERA in 1972 and organizes housewives against the amendment
Analysis of the white, church-going base she built and its racial politics
Anti-gay campaigning, opposition to AIDS education, gay-marriage scare tactics
Endorses Trump shortly before her death at 92 in 2016

notes: main_span starts at her first congressional run (1952, year from general knowledge; transcript gives no year) rather than the 1946 Bakewell campaign. Transcript says the ERA died in 1985; the ratification deadline actually lapsed in 1982. reaches_present for the Trump endorsement and the 2020 abortion-opinion discussion. Eagle Forum stands in for STOP ERA, which has no separate entry.
